chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Allah does not open for a servant a door from the affairs of the world except that He opens for him from greed the like of it.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of worldly success according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise maxim from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), illustrating the divine wisdom behind the spiritual test of provision. Scholars note that this 'opening' of greed is not merely a punishment but a proportional trial, ensuring that worldly ease does not lead to complacency but rather tests the servant's gratitude and detachment. This concept underscores the Shia understanding of the world as a transient testing ground where material blessings are inextricably linked to spiritual vigilance.
